page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.4xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance runs on an arm64 AWS Graviton processor featuring 16 dedicated physical cores based on the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture operating at 2.5 GHz with a single thread per core. Memory capacity is 64 GB, offering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4 GB of RAM allocated per physical core. A major architectural feature is the inclusion of 7500 GB of dense local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth capability of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark results show balanced throughput across multithreaded and data-centric workloads, though single-thread metrics reflect architectural tradeoffs. In multithreaded testing, the system delivers solid mid-tier output, highlighted by 24284.34 in stress-ng multi-core and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8641.0. In-memory and caching operations perform reliably, achieving 18.89 million Redis SET operations per second alongside 10366.25 in PassMark database operations. Conversely, single-core processing scores lower relative to high-frequency x86 alternatives, with Geekbench single-core reaching 947.0 and single-threaded gzip compression registering in the bottom quartile. LLM inference processing rates are similarly constrained.

By delivering 7.5 TB of integrated NVMe storage paired with dedicated Arm cores and 25 Gbps networking, the im4gn.4xlarge provides high resource density for IOPS-heavy applications without incurring the cost overhead of separate attached block storage. The instance profile is well suited for distributed NoSQL databases, log analysis clusters, real-time analytics pipelines, and caching nodes requiring high disk throughput alongside balanced compute.
description: Amazon Web Services im4gn.4xlarge is a storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by an arm64 AWS Graviton processor. It provides 16 dedicated physical cores using the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture at 2.5 GHz, paired with 64 GB of memory and 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system includes 7500 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, bypassing network-attached storage bottlenecks. Benchmark evaluations indicate stable mid-tier performance across multi-core compute, database operations, and memory workloads, while single-thread processing speed and CPU-based LLM inference are comparatively lower. The platform offers significant storage density per vCPU, making it a cost-efficient architecture for data-heavy workloads such as distributed file systems, NoSQL databases, search indexing, and real-time streaming data ingestion.
